environmental.altitude: no loss of performance to 10,000 ft (3,048 m)

features.optics-sfp-plus: 10 GbE SFP+ and 1 GbE SFP in any port
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 switches mixed with EX4200 and EX4550; the Virtual Chassis module or SFP+ ports as VCPs

management.oob: one RJ-45 management port with link and status lamps

performance.expansion-ports: up to 8 more SFP+ ports with two 4-port uplink modules
performance.sfp-plus-speeds: 10 GbE or 1 GbE on each fixed SFP+ port

physical.weight-note: 37 lb (17 kg) with one AC power supply (Table 5)

platform.software: Junos OS, first release 10.2R1 for the -FB and -BF models

power.power-input-ac: 100 to 120 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz; 12 A and 6 A
power.power-input-dc: operating range -42 to -60 VDC, nominal -48 VDC, 30 A maximum
power.power-supply-output: 1000 W at 100 to 120 VAC and 1200 W at 200 to 240 VAC; 1200 W on DC
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, load sharing; do not mix AC and DC, or front-to-back and back-to-front

thermal.fans: one fan tray with five fans; the switch runs 30 seconds while the tray is replaced

bf.description: EX4500-40F-BF: one AC supply with an orange lever and a back-to-front fan tray with the orange INTAKE label. The rest is as the -FB.

bf-c.description: EX4500-40F-BF-C: the -BF with hardware that supports Data Center Bridging. The panels are the same.

dc-c.description: EX4500-40F-DC-C: one DC supply with a green lever and a front-to-back fan tray, with Data Center Bridging. The guide lists no back-to-front DC supply.

fb.description: EX4500-40F-FB: one AC supply with a green lever and a front-to-back fan tray with the green EXHAUST label. It has a cover panel in the second supply slot, two uplink module cover panels and the intraconnect module (guide Table 3).

fb-c.description: EX4500-40F-FB-C: the -FB with hardware that supports Data Center Bridging. The panels are the same.

two-psu.description: The EX4500-40F-FB with a second AC supply in slot 1, as the guide allows. An illustration, not an order code.

vc1-bf.description: EX4500-40F-VC1-BF: the -BF-C with a Virtual Chassis module in the rear slot. The front panel prints VIRTUAL CHASSIS.

vc1-dc.description: EX4500-40F-VC1-DC: the -DC-C with a Virtual Chassis module in the rear slot. The front panel prints VIRTUAL CHASSIS.

vc1-fb.description: EX4500-40F-VC1-FB: the -FB-C with a Virtual Chassis module in the rear slot instead of the intraconnect module. The front panel prints VIRTUAL CHASSIS.

description: Juniper EX4500-40F, a 2RU 10 GbE aggregation and data-centre top-of-rack switch that runs Junos OS. The port side has 40 SFP+ ports in two rows, each taking a 10 GbE SFP+ or a 1 GbE SFP. It also has two uplink module slots with cover panels. The LCD panel has two buttons and three lamps. There is an RJ-45 console port, a management port and a USB port. The other side carries two power supply slots, one fan tray and a rear module slot. The slot takes an intraconnect module or a Virtual Chassis module. One panel serves eight models. They differ in the supply (AC or DC), the airflow and the rear module.

gaps.wanted: The part number of the mounting kit and the ear positions. The guide describes the front mounting brackets and prints no part number for them.

The 4-port SFP+ uplink module is not modelled. Each slot accepts its cover panel only. The module's ports are numbered 0 to 3 with a lamp pair each and an ST lamp (guide Figures 10 and 17). The guide prints no model number for it. A third-party tracker lists it as EX4500-UM-4XSFP, which is unconfirmed.

The Juniper part numbers of the supplies, the fan trays, the cover panels and the rear modules. The guide names them by role only. Its model numbers (EX4500-40F-FB and the others) are the only order codes.
The datasheet of the EX4500. The product page is retired and none is held, so the throughput, the power drawn and the compliance list are not stated.
Which of the two supply slots the shipped supply sits in. The guide says one supply ships and the cover panel fills the second slot; the supply is placed in slot 0.
Where the green EXHAUST or orange INTAKE label shows behind the fan tray vents. The guide says it is visible through the vents and no figure draws it.
A drawing or photograph of the supply cover panel and of the uplink module cover panel. The guide lists them in Table 3 and draws neither, so both are plain plates with two screws.
A flat drawing of the DC supply. The guide's Figure 24 is isometric, so the terminal block and the lugs are placed by assumption.
A flat drawing of the Virtual Chassis module. The guide's Figures 7 and 12 are isometric, so the positions of its lamps and its two ports are estimated and the ports are plain openings.

Whether the -FB-C, -BF-C and -DC-C models print VIRTUAL CHASSIS on the front panel. The guide says that switches with the label support DCB and that the -C models support DCB, but not that the -C models carry it. The legend is drawn on the -VC1 models alone, which is estimated.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port. It is drawn with the neutral usb2 skin.
The serial number label and the hazard marks, which the figures do not draw. The maker's marks are logos and are not drawn.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels. The guide names the protective earthing terminal on the left side and draws no flat side.

esd.description: the wrist-strap ESD point on the front panel (guide Figure 4)

attrs.redundancy-note: One fan tray of five fans. The switch stays up if one fan fails at room temperature, and the whole tray is replaced, never one fan

lcd-buttons.description: the LCD panel's Menu and Enter buttons

legends.description: printed legends that only some models carry

mgmt.mixed: the management cluster at the right of the front: an RJ-45 console, an RJ-45 management port and a USB port. Three kinds, one purpose: reaching and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: Two supply slots, labelled 1 and 0; the switch ships with one supply and a cover panel. Do not mix AC and DC supplies, or supplies of different airflow

rear-module.description: The rear slot for the intraconnect module or the Virtual Chassis module (PIC 3 in the guide's terminology table)

sfp-plus.description: Ports 0 to 39 as printed, the even ports on the upper row; each takes a 10 GbE SFP+ or a 1 GbE SFP

sfp-plus-activity-leds.description: The link and activity lamp of each SFP+ port, a triangle pointing at its port (guide Table 13)

sfp-plus-status-leds.description: The status lamp of each SFP+ port, a triangle pointing at its port (guide Table 14)

status-leds.description: The three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and MST (guide Table 10)

uplink.description: The two uplink module slots at the top of the face. Slot 1 is on the left (PIC 1) and slot 2 on the right (PIC 2)

name: ex4500-40f

airflow-colours.note: The guide's colours are not those of the EX4600 or EX4550: a supply's ejector lever is green for front-to-back airflow and orange for back-to-front, and it must match the EXHAUST (green) or INTAKE (orange) label seen through the fan tray vents.

chassis.note: Guide Table 5: 3.5 in (8.9 cm) high, 17.25 in (43.82 cm) wide, 21.1 in (53.6 cm) deep, 37 lb (17 kg) with one AC supply, 3 lb a supply. So the height is 88.9 mm, the width 438.2 mm and the depth 535.9 mm, and the switch is 2 rack units. The width is the body: the front mount brackets extend it to 19 in, so they are not modelled.

colour.note: The figures are line drawings and no photograph is held, so the chassis colour is a mid grey. It is not a paint reference.

environment.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide says the switch mounts in a two-post, a four-post or an enclosed cabinet rack with the front mounting brackets (Table 5). It prints no part number for the mounting kit and the library holds no contract for it, so chassis.ears and chassis.kits are left out and a gap says so.

fans-and-supplies.note: The two power supplies (AC front-to-back, AC back-to-front, DC front-to-back), the fan tray (front-to-back or back-to-front), and the rear module are field-replaceable units in bays. The guide gives them no Juniper part number, so each is named for its role. The supplies and the fan tray are not those of the EX4550 or the EX4600: the supplies give 1000 and 1200 W and have a C19 inlet, and the tray is one unit of five fans. The intraconnect and Virtual Chassis modules are offline units; the others are hot-swappable.

front-controls.note: Figure 4: the LCD panel on a plate at the right, 335.7 to 432.1 mm and 4.1 to 31.7 mm down, with the window 362.5 to 401.0 mm; the Menu button above the Enter button at 408.2 mm, centres 12.9 and 20.9 mm down; the three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and MST at 415.5 mm, 9.8, 13.6 and 17.3 mm down; and below the plate, at the right, a stacked pair in one frame, the RJ-45 console CON above the RJ-45 management port MGMT (centres 402.1 mm, 59.4 and 73.4 mm down), a vertical USB port at 417.4 mm and the ESD point at 428.3 mm. The guide names the three as the console port, the management port and the USB port; it has no mini-USB console port.

gate-1.note: Figure 4 (the front panel, a drawing whose face is flat under a roof seen at an angle) was rendered at 1200 dpi. The face measures 5024 x 1003 px, an aspect of 5.01 against the table's 438.2 / 88.9 = 4.93, 1.6 percent out, so it is read as orthographic at 0.0872 mm per pixel across and 0.0886 down. Figure 6 (the rear) measures 1930 x 380 display px, 5.08, 3 percent out. No photograph is held. Every position read off a figure is estimated, to about 0.5 mm on the front and 1 mm on the rear.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life notice. Juniper's own page was not reached and the guide, modified 2017-10-18, states none. A third-party tracker (endoflife.ai) lists end of support at 2016-01-31 for the -FB and -BF, 2018-12-31 for the -C models and 2022-12-31 for the VC1 models, with no end-of-sale date. The latest is carried and it is estimated.

maker-mark.note: Figure 4 prints the maker's logo on the LCD plate. It is not drawn: it has a reserved logo zone, and the plain model name EX4500 is drawn as text.

port-lamps.note: Figure 4, Figure 16 and Tables 13 and 14: four triangular lamps in the band between the two cages of each column, each pointing at its port. The lamps left to right are the link and activity lamp of the lower port (down-pointing), the link and activity lamp of the upper port (up-pointing), the status lamp of the lower port and the status lamp of the upper port, in the order of the guide's labels in Figure 16. The centres are 2.9, 5.7, 9.2 and 11.9 mm from the column edge and 66.9 mm down; the lamp is 2.25 x 2.0 mm, the library's small triangle.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off Figure 4: the even numerals of the upper ports are above the upper cage and the odd numerals of the lower ports are below the lower cage, each over the middle of its column, so a block reads 0 2 above and 1 3 below. The ports are 0 to 39 as printed. Interface names are not printed on the unit. The guide's terminology table maps the 40 network ports to PIC 0, the left uplink slot to PIC 1 and the right to PIC 2, with xe interfaces; the interface names go here and not in the manifest.

ports.note: Figure 4, callout "Network ports": 40 SFP+ ports in ten blocks of two columns, each column a stacked pair. The columns are 171 px, 14.9 mm, apart in the drawing, 4.5 percent over the registry's 14.25 mm pitch, so the registry pitch is used with the blocks centred in their frames. The frames start 38.1 mm apart: the cells start at 18.1 mm and 38.1 mm on, so the gutter is 38.1 - 2 x 14.25 = 9.6 mm. The rows are 15.8 mm apart at the opening centres, 5 percent over the registry's 15.0 mm; the upper cell starts at 53.5 mm and the lower at 69.3 mm. The cells use the registry's aperture, 14.25 x 10.4.

power.note: Table 40 (AC): 100 to 120 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 12 A and 6 A, 1000 W and 1200 W output. Table 42 (DC): -42 to -60 VDC, nominal -48 VDC, 30 A maximum, 1200 W output. The guide gives no figure for the power the switch draws, and the rows for the fans' power are empty.

rear-layout.note: Figure 6, read at 0.227 mm across and 0.234 down per display pixel: two power supply slots stacked at the left, slot 1 above slot 0 (Figure 6 labels them 1 and 0 on the fan tray), each about 76 mm by 40 mm; a rear module strip over the fan tray, 345.9 x 21.7 mm; and the fan tray below it, 352.5 x 63.1 mm, with a handle at each end. The guide does not say which slot the shipped supply is in; the supply is placed in slot 0 and the cover panel in slot 1.

sources.note: Juniper EX4500 Switch Hardware Guide, modified 2017-10-18, 326 pages (Juniper Networks, copyright 2017): Table 3 (the models), Table 5 (the chassis), Figures 4 to 7 (the panels), Tables 6 to 14 (the LCD panel and the lamps), Tables 15 to 17 (the airflow and the lamps of the supplies), Tables 40 and 42 (the power figures) and the environment table (Table 35). The guide was supplied as a PDF; no live public URL for it is held, and the guide's own pathway page now serves a moved-page notice. No datasheet of the EX4500 is held; the product page is retired. The held intake folders for the EX and QFX lines were read: they hold no studio photograph, stencil or 3D model of the EX4500, and the guide's figures are the only drawings. Terms: the document is Juniper's, read here for facts only, and nothing of it is copied into the library.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md): a row pair is the upper cage upright over the lower turned 180, so both lips face the band between the two cages. Figure 4 is a line drawing that draws the release tab at the foot of both cages, and a line drawing cannot say which way the metal faces, so the convention is kept and a photograph of the real panel would overturn it.

uplink-slots.note: Figures 4 and 9: two uplink module slots at the top of the face, PIC 1 at the left and PIC 2 at the right, 151.0 x 40.8 mm. Table 3 says each model ships with two uplink module cover panels; the figures draw the 4-port SFP+ module in place instead. UPLINK MODULES ARE NOT MODELLED: this slice builds no module family, so each slot is a bay that accepts the cover panel alone. The cover panel is drawn as a plain plate with two screws, because no figure draws it. The module (4 SFP+ ports, labelled ST) is named here and in a gap.

variants.note: Table 3: the eight models are EX4500-40F-FB, -BF, -FB-C, -BF-C, -DC-C, -VC1-FB, -VC1-BF and -VC1-DC. One front panel serves all eight. The guide says that switches with the label VIRTUAL CHASSIS on the front panel support Data Center Bridging (the note under Table 3 and Figure 5, "Label Identifying EX4500 Switches that Support DCB"). That is a one-way statement: Table 3 marks the -FB-C, -BF-C, -DC-C and the three -VC1 models as supporting DCB, and the guide does not say whether the -C models carry the label too. The label is drawn on the -VC1 models alone; that choice is estimated, not stated by the guide. The airflow, the supply and the rear module differ.

vents.note: Figure 4: a honeycomb field at the left end of the panel from 3.6 to 15.6 mm, a strip along the foot from 18 to 390 mm and a strip between the two uplink slots, all declared vents. The field inside each uplink slot belongs to the module and is not chassis. The guide gives the air intake as the front vents for front-to-back and the rear vents for back-to-front.

bottom.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide's figures show no underside and no photograph is held.

placements.description: Table 10 - red: major alarm; amber: minor alarm; unlit: no alarm or the switch is halted
Table 10 - green steady: Junos OS loaded; green blinking: the switch is booting; unlit: off or halted
Table 10 - standalone: green steady when working; Virtual Chassis: green steady master, blinking backup, unlit line card
Tables 11 and 12 - the link and activity lamp is green steady with a link and blinking with traffic; the status lamp blinks once a second at 10 Mbps, twice at 100 Mbps and three times at 1000 Mbps

left.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide names the protective earthing terminal on the left side, with a pair of threaded inserts near the rear corner at 15.86 mm spacing, and draws no flat side wall.

right.empty: Not drawn by any source held. No figure shows the right wall flat.

top.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide shows the roof only at an angle in its front figures and no photograph is held.
